```{r slide1, echo=FALSE, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE, fig.width=12, fig.height=5, dpi=300, out.width="100%"}
# Load necessary libraries
library(tidyverse)
library(viridis)
library(maps)
library(plotly)
library(dplyr)
library(ggplot2)

# Load the dataset
u5mr = read.csv("data/final_u5mr.csv")

# Clean column names by removing the "X" prefix from year columns
names(u5mr) = gsub("^X", "", names(u5mr))

u5mr <- u5mr %>%
  mutate(Country.Name = case_when(
    Country.Name == "Antigua and Barbuda" ~ "Antigua",
    Country.Name == "Bolivia (Plurinational State of)" ~ "Bolivia",
    Country.Name == "Brunei Darussalam" ~ "Brunei",
    Country.Name == "Côte d'Ivoire" ~ "Ivory Coast",
    Country.Name == "Congo" ~ "Republic of Congo",
    Country.Name == "Cabo Verde" ~ "Cape Verde",
    Country.Name == "Czechia" ~ "Czech Republic",
    Country.Name == "Micronesia (Federated States of)" ~ "Micronesia",
    Country.Name == "United Kingdom" ~ "UK",
    Country.Name == "Iran (Islamic Republic of)" ~ "Iran",
    Country.Name == "Saint Kitts and Nevis" ~ "Saint Kitts",
    Country.Name == "Republic of Korea" ~ "South Korea",
    Country.Name == "Lao People's Democratic Republic" ~ "Laos",
    Country.Name == "Republic of Moldova" ~ "Moldova",
    Country.Name == "Netherlands (Kingdom of the)" ~ "Netherlands",
    Country.Name == "Democratic People's Republic of Korea" ~ "North Korea",
    Country.Name == "State of Palestine" ~ "Palestine",
    Country.Name == "Kosovo (UNSCR 1244)" ~ "Kosovo",
    Country.Name == "Russian Federation" ~ "Russia",
    Country.Name == "Eswatini" ~ "Swaziland",
    Country.Name == "Syrian Arab Republic" ~ "Syria",
    Country.Name == "Trinidad and Tobago" ~ "Trinidad",
    Country.Name == "Tuvalu" ~ "Tuvalu",
    Country.Name == "Türkiye" ~ "Turkey",
    Country.Name == "United Republic of Tanzania" ~ "Tanzania",
    Country.Name == "United States" ~ "USA",
    Country.Name == "Saint Vincent and the Grenadines" ~ "Saint Vincent",
    Country.Name == "British Virgin Islands" ~ "Virgin Islands",
    Country.Name == "Venezuela (Bolivarian Republic of)" ~ "Venezuela",
    Country.Name == "Viet Nam" ~ "Vietnam",
    TRUE ~ Country.Name
  ))
  
# Get map data
world_map = map_data("world")

# Create full-screen background world map with text overlay
slide1_plot <- ggplot() +
  # Draw the world map
  geom_polygon(data = world_map,
               aes(x = long, y = lat, group = group),
               fill = "#a6bddb", color = NA, linewidth = 0, alpha = 0.3) +
  coord_fixed(1.3, 
              xlim = c(-180, 180), 
              ylim = c(-90, 90), 
              expand = FALSE) +
  theme_void() +
  geom_vline(xintercept = seq(-180, 180, by = 30), color = "gray90", linewidth = 0.1) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = seq(-90, 90, by = 30), color = "gray90", linewidth = 0.1)

# Save your full-screen map plot
ggsave("map_background.png", plot = slide1_plot, width = 16, height = 9, dpi = 300)
```

class: title_slide1

# The Geography of Survival
## Understanding Child Mortality Worldwide
### Where the child is born can determine whether they survive

Author: Dilys Huynh

---
.title_slide[
Where Are Children Most Vulnerable?
]
.insight_text2[
The map illustrates a significant disparity in child survival across the globe. Regions in **Sub-Saharan Africa** and parts of **South Asia** exhibit considerably higher under-five mortality rates, which is often often exceeding 50 deaths per 1000 live births. Notably, **Niger** in Sub-Saharan Africa is highlighted in yellow, indicating one of the highest U5MR globally (over 100 deaths per 1,000 live births). In contrast, much of **North America**, **Europe, and East Asia** demonstrates significantly lower rates, typically below 10 deaths per 1,000 live births. 

This suggests that a child’s place of birth continues to be a critical determinant of their chances of surviving to their fifth birthday—highlighting persistent challenges in wealth, healthcare infrastructure, and access to basic services.
]
.title_plot2[
Under-Five Mortality Rates by Country (2023)
]

.plot2[
```{r slide2, echo=FALSE, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE, fig.width=12, fig.height=5.5, dpi=300, out.width="100%"}

# Prepare under-five mortality data for 2023
u5mr_2023 = u5mr %>%
  filter(Uncertainty.Bounds. == "Median") %>%
  select(ISO.Code, Country.Name, "2023", Uncertainty.Bounds.) %>%
  rename(MortalityRate = "2023") %>%
  mutate(MortalityRate = as.numeric(MortalityRate))

# Merge mortality data with map
map_data_2023 = world_map %>%
  left_join(u5mr_2023, by = c("region" = "Country.Name"))

slide2_plot = ggplot(map_data_2023, aes(x = long, y = lat, group = group, fill = MortalityRate,
                                        text = paste0("Country: ", region, "<br>",
                "Mortality Rate: ", round(MortalityRate, 2), " deaths/1,000"))) +
  geom_polygon(color = "gray80", size = 0.2) +
  scale_fill_viridis(option = "plasma", na.value = "lightgray", name = "Deaths per 1,000") +
  theme_void() +
  theme(
    plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0.7, size = 14, face = "bold", color = "#003366"),
    axis.title.x = element_text(size = 9),
    axis.title.y = element_text(size = 9)
  )

slide2_plot = ggplotly(slide2_plot, tooltip = "text") %>%
  layout(
    xaxis = list(visible = FALSE, showgrid = FALSE, zeroline = FALSE, tickvals = NULL),
    yaxis = list(visible = FALSE, showgrid = FALSE, zeroline = FALSE, tickvals = NULL),
    #plot_bgcolor = 'rgba(0,0,0,0)',

    height = 530,
    width = 1100
  )
```

.title_slide[
Declining Child Mortality: A Global Trend
]
.plot[
```{r slide3, echo=FALSE, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}

live_birth_data = read.csv("data/livebirth.csv")
live_birth_data = live_birth_data %>%
  select(-X)

names(live_birth_data) = gsub("^X", "", names(live_birth_data))

live_birth_long = live_birth_data %>%
  pivot_longer(
    cols = `1960`:`2023`,
    names_to = "Year",
    values_to = "Live_Births"
  ) %>%
  mutate(Year = as.numeric(Year)) %>%
  filter(Year >= 2000 & Year <= 2023)

u5mr_long = u5mr %>%
  pivot_longer(cols = "2000":"2023", names_to = "Year", values_to = "U5MR") %>%
  mutate(Year = as.numeric(Year))

liveBirth_u5mr_data = u5mr_long %>%
  inner_join(live_birth_long, by = c("Country.Name", "Year")) %>%
  mutate(Estimated_Under_Five_Deaths = (U5MR / 1000) * Live_Births)

# Summing U5MR for each region and year
region_sum = liveBirth_u5mr_data %>%
  group_by(SDG.Region, Year) %>%
  filter(Year == c("2000", "2005", "2010", "2015", "2020", "2023")) %>%
  summarize(Total_Deaths = sum(Estimated_Under_Five_Deaths, na.rm = TRUE),
            Total_Live_Births = sum(Live_Births, na.rm = TRUE),
            .groups = 'drop') %>%
  mutate(
    Regional_U5MR = (Total_Deaths / Total_Live_Births) * 1000
  ) %>%
  filter(Year %in% c(2000, 2005, 2010, 2015, 2020, 2023))
  
  

# Create the plot with all countries and regions
slide3_plot = plot_ly(
  data = region_sum,
  x = ~Year,
  y = ~Regional_U5MR,
  type = 'scatter',
  mode = 'lines+markers',
  color = ~SDG.Region,  
  line = list(width = 1.5),
  marker = list(size = 4),
  text = ~paste0("Region: ", SDG.Region, 
                 "<br>Year: ", Year,
                 "<br>U5MR: ", round(Regional_U5MR, 1)),
  hoverinfo = "text",
  showlegend = TRUE
) %>%
  layout(
    xaxis = list(
      title = list(
        text = "Year",
        font = list(size = 11)
      )
    ),
    yaxis = list(
      title = list(
        text = "Under-Five Mortality Rate (per 1,000 live births)",
        font = list(size = 11)
      )
    ),
    hovermode = "closest",
    height = 420,
    width = 1100
  )

slide3_plot
```
]
.title_plot3[
Regional Trends in Under-Five Mortality (2000–2023)
]
.insight_text3[
At the beginning of the 21st century, **Sub-Saharan Africa** faced the highest burden of under-five mortality, with Regional U5MR nearly 140 deaths per 1000 live births. In contrast, **Europe and Northern America** consistently had the lowest rates, beginning around 10 deaths per 1,000 live births. Over the next 23 years, all regions saw a significant and consistent decrease in their U5MR. Specifically, **Sub-Saharan Africa** remained the region with the highest rate, but it saw a substantial decline, dropping from 125 to approximately 85 deaths per 1,000 live births by 2023. 

However, between 2020 and 2023, the U5MR moderately increased across all regions. This widespread setback likely reflects the disruptive impact of the COVID-19 pandemic, climate change, or regional conflicts, highlighting the fragility of global health gains.
]

.title_slide4[
Can Wealth Save Lives? Poverty's Impact on Child Mortality
]

.plot4[
```{r slide4, echo=FALSE, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
gdp_data = read.csv("data/GDP.csv", header = TRUE, fill = TRUE, check.names = TRUE)

names(gdp_data) = gsub("^X", "", names(gdp_data))

gdp_data = gdp_data[, colnames(gdp_data) != ""]

gdp_long = gdp_data %>%
  pivot_longer(
    cols = `1960`:`2024`,            
    names_to = "Year",
    values_to = "GDP_Per_Capita"
  ) %>%
  mutate(Year = as.numeric(Year))

gdp_u5mr_data = u5mr_long %>%
  inner_join(gdp_long, by = c("Country.Name", "Year"))

# Basic scatter plot colored by region
region_sum_gdp = gdp_u5mr_data %>%
  group_by(SDG.Region) %>%
  summarize(
    avg_gdp = mean(GDP_Per_Capita, na.rm = TRUE), 
    avg_u5mr = mean(U5MR, na.rm = TRUE),

region_sum_gdp = region_sum_gdp %>%

slide4_plot = plot_ly(region_sum_gdp) %>%
  add_markers(

    y = ~avg_u5mr,

                   "<br>Average U5MR: ", round(avg_u5mr, 2), " deaths / 1,000"),
    color = ~Region,       
    marker = list(size = 10),
    hoverinfo = "text"
  ) %>%
  layout(
    xaxis = list(
      title = list(
        text = "(Log) GDP per Capita (USD)",
        font = list(size = 11)
      )
    ),
    yaxis = list(

        text = "Under-Five Mortality Rate (per 1,000 live births)",

      )
    ),

    height = 450,
    width = 1100
  )

slide4_plot 
```
]
.title_plot4[
GDP Per Capita vs Under-Five Mortality Rate
]
.insight_text_slide4[
This scatter plot illustrates a clear inverse relationship between a region's GDP and its U5MR. Regions with higher average GDP per capita, such as **Europe and Northern America** average GDP over $33,000, report the lowest child mortality rates, while regions like **Sub-Saharan Africa** average GDP around $2,000 and **Central and Southern Asia** average GDP around $2,600 have significantly lower economic means and face the highest burden. 
This strong inverse relationship highlights how wealth is a powerful determinant of child survival, pointing to the need for equity-focused investment in health infrastructure and social services in low-income regions.
]
---
.title_slide[
Educated Mothers, Healthier Children: The Role of Schooling
]
.title_plot[
Maternal Education vs Under-Five Mortality Rate
]
```{r slide5, echo=FALSE, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}

education_data = read.csv("data/mean-years-of-schooling-female .csv")

education_u5mr_data = u5mr_long %>% 
  filter(Uncertainty.Bounds. == "Median") %>%
  inner_join(education_data, by = c("Country.Name", "Year"))

education_u5mr_data = education_u5mr_data %>%
  rename(
    Maternal_Education = Mean.years.of.schooling..ISCED.1.or.higher...population.25..years..female
  ) %>%
  filter(!is.na(Maternal_Education), !is.na(U5MR))

education_u5mr_data = education_u5mr_data %>%
  arrange(Maternal_Education)

# Fit the linear model for regression
lm_model = lm(U5MR ~ Maternal_Education, data = education_u5mr_data)
predicted_values = predict(lm_model, education_u5mr_data)

slide5_plot = plot_ly(education_u5mr_data) %>%
  add_markers(
    x = ~Maternal_Education,
    y = ~U5MR,
    text = ~paste0("Country: ", Country.Name, 
                   "<br>Year: ", Year,
                   "<br>Maternal Education: ", round(Maternal_Education, 2), " yrs",
                   "<br>Average Under-Five Mortality Rate: ", round(U5MR, 2), " deaths/1,000"),
    color = ~SDG.Region,       
    marker = list(size = 10),
    hoverinfo = "text"
  ) %>%
  add_lines(
    x = ~Maternal_Education,
    y = predicted_values,
    line = list(color = "red", width = 2),
    name = "Regression Line"
  ) %>%
  layout(
    xaxis = list(
      title = list(
        text = "Average Years of Maternal Education",
        font = list(size = 11)
      )
    ),
    yaxis = list(
      title = list(
        text = "Under-Five Mortality Rate (per 1,000 live births)",
        font = list(size = 11)
      )
    ),
    hovermode = "closest",
    showlegend = TRUE,
    height = 440,
    width = 1100
  )

slide5_plot
```
.insight_text_slide5[
In **Sub-Saharan Africa**, where women aged 25+ often have 0–6 years of schooling, U5MR frequently exceeds 100 deaths per 1,000 live births, with some data points approaching 250 deaths. In contrast, regions like **Europe and Northern America** and parts of **Eastern and South-Eastern Asia** show 12–14 years of maternal education and U5MR consistently below 10 per 1,000. Countries in the 4–8 year education range exhibit intermediate U5MR (typically 30–70 per 1,000), reflecting a gradual decline with increased education.
The regression line visually reinforces this inverse relationship, emphasizing maternal education as a key lever for improving child survival and public health outcomes globally.
]
---
.title_slide6[
Access to Survive: Water and Sanitation's Impact
]
.insight_text_slide6[
Despite global improvements, significant regional disparities persist in access to basic water and sanitation services in 2022.
* In **Sub-Saharan Africa**, sanitation coverage is below 50% in most countries, with some falling below 20%. Similarly, water access often remains under 60%, particularly in Central and Eastern African regions. In contrast, **Europe**, **North America**, and **East Asia** achieve nearly universal access, which is often 90–100% for both services.
Countries like India and Indonesia show a mismatch between service: higher water access (~90%) but lower sanitation coverage (~60%), indicating slower progress in hygiene infrastructure. 
* Globally, sanitation access lags behind water, particularly in rural areas, emphasizing the need for integrated solutions.
* These disparities reflect urgent needs for infrastructure investment, public health interventions, and policies that treat sanitation and water access as a basic human right.
]
.title_plot6[
Percentage of Population with Access to Basic Sanitation and Water Services (2022)
]
.plot6[

```{r slide6, echo=FALSE, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
#Merge data

# Plot sanitizer map
```

.title_slide[
The Helping Hand: Healthcare Access and Child Mortality
]

.plot[
```{r slide7, echo=FALSE, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
# Get doctor data
doctor_data = read.csv("data/doctors.csv")
doctor_data = doctor_data %>%
  rename(
    codeCountry = SpatialDimValueCode,
    doctorCount = FactValueNumeric,
    Year = Period
  ) %>%
  mutate(Profession = "Doctor")

# Get nurse data
nurse_data = read.csv("data/nurse.csv")
nurse_data = nurse_data %>%
  rename(
    codeCountry = SpatialDimValueCode,
    nurseCount = FactValueNumeric,
    Year = Period
  ) %>%
  mutate(Profession = "Nurse")

# Merge doctor and nurse data
doctor_nurse_data = bind_rows(doctor_data, nurse_data) %>%
  select(codeCountry, Location, Year, Value, Profession) %>%
  pivot_wider(
    names_from = Profession,
    values_from = Value
  ) %>%
  rename(
    Country.Name = Location,
    doctorCount = Doctor,
    nurseCount = Nurse
  )

# Calculate average for each country and replace NA with average if needed
doctor_nurse_avg = doctor_nurse_data %>%
  filter(Year == max(Year, na.rm = TRUE)) %>%
  group_by(codeCountry) %>%
  mutate(
    doctorCount = ifelse(is.na(doctorCount), mean(doctorCount, na.rm = TRUE), doctorCount),
    nurseCount = ifelse(is.na(nurseCount), mean(nurseCount, na.rm = TRUE), nurseCount)
  ) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  mutate(
    doctorCount = ifelse(is.na(doctorCount), mean(doctorCount, na.rm = TRUE), doctorCount),
    nurseCount = ifelse(is.na(nurseCount), mean(nurseCount, na.rm = TRUE), nurseCount)
  )

# Join data
health_u5mr_data = u5mr_long %>% 
  filter(Uncertainty.Bounds. == "Median") %>%
  inner_join(doctor_nurse_avg, by = c("Country.Name", "Year"))

# Plot the facet scatter plot for health factor
doctor_nurse_long = health_u5mr_data %>%
  select(Country.Name, SDG.Region, Year, doctorCount, nurseCount, U5MR) %>%
  pivot_longer(cols = c(doctorCount, nurseCount),
               names_to = "Profession",
               values_to = "CountPer10000"
               ) %>%
  mutate(
    Profession = recode(Profession,
                             doctorCount = "Doctors",
                             nurseCount = "Nurses"),
    text = paste0(
      "Country: ", Country.Name,
      "<br>Profession: ", Profession,
      "<br>Count per 10,000: ", round(CountPer10000, 2),
      "<br>U5MR: ", round(U5MR, 2)
    )
  )

slide7_plot = ggplot(doctor_nurse_long, 
                     aes(x = CountPer10000, y = U5MR, color = Profession, text = text, group = Profession)) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.7, size = 3) +
  geom_smooth(method = "lm", se = FALSE, linewidth = 0.8) +
  facet_wrap(~ SDG.Region) +
  labs(
    x = "Healthcare Workers per 10,000",
    y = "Under-5 Mortality Rate (per 1,000 live births)",
    color = "Profession"
  ) +
  scale_color_manual(values = c("Doctors" = "#1f77b4", "Nurses" = "#ff7f0e")) +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(
    axis.title.x = element_text(size = 9),
    axis.title.y = element_text(size = 9),  
    strip.text = element_text(face = "bold", size = 10)
  )

slide7_plot = ggplotly(slide7_plot, tooltip = "text") %>%
  layout(
    height = 450,
    width = 1100
    )

slide7_plot
```
]
.title_plot7[
U5MR vs. Healthcare Workers by Region and Profession
]
.insight_text[
The faceted scatter plot shows the relationship between the number of healthcare workers and the U5MR, **Sub-Saharan Africa** demonstrates the most significant inverse correlation. A critical shortage of healthcare workers (fewer than 50), is associated with a very high U5MR, ranging from 60 to 120 deaths per 1,000 live births. Conversely, **Europe and North America** possess an abundant number of healthcare workers, typically exceeding total 100 per 10,000 population, while maintaining an extremely low U5MR, generally below 10. The remaining regions across the globe also exhibit a similar trend, where an increase in the number of healthcare workers is linked to a reduction in the U5MR, underscoring the pivotal role of the healthcare workforce in improving child health and minimizing mortality rates on a global scale.
]
---
.title_slide[
Progress and Challenges in Sub-Saharan Africa's Child Mortality
]
.insight_text_slide8[
In the group with the highest U5MR in 2000, **Niger** topped the list with 225 deaths per 1,000 children. By 2023, this number had decreased to nearly 115, but **Niger** still held the highest position in the region.  Similarly, the rate of **Nigeria**, **Somalia**, **Chad**, and **South Sudan** all decreased by around 70 deaths. Although all five countries showed significant improvements, they still ranked among those with the highest U5MR in 2023. On the other hand, five countries with the lowest U5MR in 2000 mostly showed positive progress, except for one notable exception. **Seychelles** was the only country in this group where the mortality rate slightly increased, going against the general trend. The other countries such as **Gabon, Mauritius, Sao Tome and Principe, and Cape Verde** all had substantial reductions. Overall, the chart shows that most countries in **Sub-Saharan Africa** have made significant progress in reducing child mortality, but there remain specific challenges in certain areas.
]
.title_plot[
Top and Bottom 5 Countries in Sub-Saharan Africa (2000 vs 2023)
]
.plot8[
```{r slide8, echo=FALSE, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}

# Get the data for Sub-Saharan Region
sub_saharan_u5mr <- u5mr_long %>%
  select(ISO.Code, Country.Name, SDG.Region, Uncertainty.Bounds., Year, U5MR) %>%
  filter(SDG.Region == "Sub-Saharan Africa",
         Uncertainty.Bounds.== "Median",
         Year %in% c(2000, 2023)
  )
# Get the data for year 2000 and 2023
sub_saharan_2023 = sub_saharan_u5mr %>%
  filter(Year == 2023) %>%
  arrange(desc(U5MR)) %>%
  rename(U5MR_2023 = U5MR)

sub_saharan_2000 = sub_saharan_u5mr %>%
  filter(Year == 2000) %>% 
  select(ISO.Code, Country.Name, U5MR) %>%
  rename(U5MR_2000 = U5MR)

# Combine top and bottom 5 countries
top_5_high = head(sub_saharan_2023, 5)
top_5_low = tail(sub_saharan_2023, 5)
selected_countries <- c(top_5_high$Country.Name, top_5_low$Country.Name)

# Filter data for selected countries and years
sub_saharan_2000_2023 = sub_saharan_2023 %>%
  left_join(sub_saharan_2000, by = "Country.Name") %>%
  filter(Country.Name %in% selected_countries) %>%
  select(Country.Name, U5MR_2023, U5MR_2000) %>%
  pivot_longer(
    cols = starts_with("U5MR"),
    names_to = "U5MR_Year",
    values_to = "U5MR"
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    Year = gsub("U5MR_", "", U5MR_Year),
    Year = as.factor(Year),
    Top_Category = case_when(
      Country.Name %in% top_5_high$Country.Name ~ "Top High",
      Country.Name %in% top_5_low$Country.Name ~ "Top Low"),
    Category_Year = paste(Top_Category, Year, sep = "_")
  )

country_order <- sub_saharan_2023 %>%
  filter(Country.Name %in% selected_countries) %>%
  arrange(desc(U5MR_2023)) %>%
  pull(Country.Name)
  
# Order countries based on 2023 U5MR for better visualization
sub_saharan_2000_2023$Country.Name <- factor(sub_saharan_2000_2023$Country.Name, 
                                             levels = country_order)

# Plot the data
slide8_plot <- sub_saharan_2000_2023 %>%
  plot_ly(x = ~Country.Name,
          y = ~U5MR,
          color = ~Category_Year,
          colors = c("Top High_2000" = "#d73027", 
                     "Top Low_2000" = "#fc8d59",
                     "Top High_2023" = "#1a9850", 
                     "Top Low_2023" = "#91cf60"),
          text = ~paste0("Country: ", Country.Name,
                         "<br>Year: ", Year,
                         "<br>U5MR: ", sprintf("%.1f", U5MR)),
          hoverinfo = "text") %>%
  add_bars(name = ~Category_Year) %>%
  layout(
    xaxis = list(
      title = list(
        text = "",
        font = list(size = 11)
      )
    ),
    yaxis = list(
      title = list(
        text = "Under-Five Mortality Rate (per 1,000 live births)",
        font = list(size = 11)
      )
    ),
    barmode = "group",
    showlegend = TRUE,
    height = 430,
    width = 1100
  )

slide8_plot
```

.title_slide[
The Changing Landscape: Progress and Persistent Challenges
]
.title_plot6[
Reduction in Under-Five Mortality Rates by Country (2000–2023)
]
.plot9[
```{r slide9, echo=FALSE, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
# Get U5MR in 2000 and 2023 for each country
u5mr_change = u5mr_long%>%
  filter(Uncertainty.Bounds. == "Median", Year %in% c(2000, 2023)) %>%
  select(Country.Name, Year, U5MR) %>%
  pivot_wider(
    names_from = Year,
    values_from = U5MR,
    names_prefix = "U5MR_") %>% 
  mutate(Change = U5MR_2000 - U5MR_2023) %>%
  arrange(desc(Change)) %>%
  drop_na()

change_map_data = world_map %>%
  left_join(u5mr_change, by = c("region" = "Country.Name")) %>%
  mutate(hover_text = paste0(region, "<br>Reduction: ", round(Change, 2), " deaths per 1,000"))

# Compute increased countries
increased_countries = change_map_data %>%
  filter(Change < 0) %>%
  group_by(region) %>%
  summarize(
    long = mean(long, na.rm = TRUE),
    lat = mean(lat, na.rm = TRUE),
    Change = mean(Change, na.rm = TRUE),
    hover_text = paste0(region, "<br>U5MR increased by: ", round(-Change, 2), " deaths per 1,000"),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  distinct(region, long, lat, Change, .keep_all = TRUE)

slide9_plot = ggplot(change_map_data,
                      aes(x = long, y = lat,
                          group = group,
                          fill = Change,
                          text = hover_text)) +
  geom_polygon(color = "gray80", size = 0.2) +
  coord_fixed(1.5) +
  scale_fill_gradient2(
    low = "red",
    mid = "white",
    high = "green", 
    midpoint = median(u5mr_change$Change),
    limits = range(u5mr_change$Change, na.rm = TRUE),
    name = "Reduction in U5MR"
  ) +
  geom_point(
    data = increased_countries,
    aes(x = long, y = lat, text = hover_text),
    color = "black",
    fill = "red",
    size = 2,
    shape = 21,
    stroke = 0.5,
    inherit.aes = FALSE
  ) +
  theme_void()
  
slide9_plot = ggplotly(slide9_plot, tooltip = "text") %>%
  layout(
    xaxis = list(visible = FALSE, showgrid = FALSE, zeroline = FALSE, tickvals = NULL),
    yaxis = list(visible = FALSE, showgrid = FALSE, zeroline = FALSE, tickvals = NULL),
    height = 450,
    width = 1100
  )

slide9_plot
```
]
.insight_text_slide9[
Countries shaded in dark green have made the most progress, with **Sub-Saharan Africa** seeing reductions of up to 60–80 deaths per 1,000 live births in many nations, reflecting the impact of effective public health programs. **Southeast Asia** has also achieved notable improvements, with several countries recording steady declines in U5MR, demonstrating regional efforts in expanding healthcare access and maternal-child health services.
However, the red dots indicate concerning regions where U5MR has increased, such as Dominica (+16.11 deaths), highlighting severe inequalities in access to healthcare. Targeted public health interventions are needed to sustain global progress and support countries that are falling behind.
]

---
.conclusion_slide[
Conclusion and Key Takeaways
]

.conclusion_text[
Significant progress has been achieved globally in reducing under-five mortality rates between 2000 and 2023. Many countries, particularly in **Sub-Saharan Africa**, have made remarkable strides, reflecting improvements in:
- Access to healthcare services  
- Sanitation and clean water  
- Female education and empowerment  
- Economic development

However, challenges remain. Some countries have experienced **increases or stagnation** in mortality rates, highlighting persistent disparities driven by. **To sustain and accelerate progress**, it is essential to:  
- Implement targeted, context-specific interventions  
- Strengthen health infrastructure and workforce  
- Promote equitable access to basic services  
- Utilize continuous data monitoring for informed policy decisions  

Ultimately, achieving global child survival goals requires **collaborative efforts** from governments, international agencies, and communities to ensure every child has the opportunity to survive and thrive.
]
